# the update, run until a pass changes nothing; that pass:
$ FIXTURE_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test  # strip-a

$ edit b/testdata/hypercase.json  # a copy of b's registry, recording parse as a bytes lift
$ edit testdata/export/prices.txtar  # a product parse doesn't make, in parse's cell, which a gaps line marks
$ go test  # strip-a
    the registries that own or use the lift parse differ in bytes:
          bytes:
            .: false
            ./b: true
        Every package that owns or uses a lift registers one declaration of it: a package that only uses a bytes lift tells by its own declaration whether an update writes the lift's cell, and so the cells past it. Declare the lift once, in a package the others import, and register that declaration. If they register one declaration already, a registry is stale: run FIXTURE_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test ./..., which rewrites the registry of every package with tests.
    testdata/export/prices.txtar: no registry claims via/parse/quote/A1: no bytes lift named parse runs over the corpus export.
        If a bytes lift should write them, register it. If not, first settle whether parse is a bytes lift, on which the registries differ, as the check's failures on them say, then run the check again: until they agree, it can't tell whether gaps line 1, which marks a cell of theirs, keeps strip from removing them.
    what ran, in order:
        import ran
        parse ran on prices
        resolve ran on prices
        import ran
        parse ran on prices
        resolve ran on prices
        import ran
        parse ran on prices
        resolve ran on prices
        parse ran on plain
        resolve ran on plain
        parse ran on plain
        resolve ran on plain
